To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the wake characteristics of a fixed and floating wind turbine model in a wind tunnel are substantially influenced by the turbulent inflow conditions and that tip vortices are not the only source for the turbulent kinetic energy in the wake.
the wake development of a fixed turbine and of a floating turbine is different under high turbulence inflow generated with the active grid.
the wake of a floating wind turbines is less organized than the wake of a fixed turbine, and the wake of a wind turbine is less organized in high turbulence inflow than in low turbulence inflow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of wake turbulence of floating wind turbine models in comparison to a bottom fixed model.
the development of a floating turbine in a turbulent inflow, which can be used as reference for the validation of CFD codes.
the wake development of a wind turbine under different turbulence conditions, that are of interest for the development of floating wind turbines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a floating turbine in low turbulence inflow generates a wake that is more stable than the wake of a fixed turbine.
the wake of floating wind turbines under high turbulence inflow is more complex than the fixed turbine.
the wake of a wind turbine is highly influenced by the inflow conditions, and that the turbine type has a subordinated role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
under low turbulence inflow the wake of a fixed turbine is characterized by tip and root vorticities, that are inhibited by the floating platform.

the wake of floating wind turbines under low turbulence inflow conditions is more stable, when compared to a fixed turbine, whereas the opposite behavior was found under high turbulence inflow conditions.
the wake of floating wind turbines in low turbulence is dominated by tip vortices, whereas the wake of a fixed turbine in low turbulence is defined by the formation of root and tip vortices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the wake of a wind turbine is not only influenced by the turbine type, but also by the inflow turbulence.
, in contrast to the wake of bottom fixed wind turbines, the wake of floating wind turbines are less stable under low turbulence conditions.
the wake of a floating turbine in free pitch is more sensitive to the inflow turbulence intensity, than to the type of turbine, when compared to a bottom fixed turbine in fixed pitch.
